Search the web to identify bands that match ALL of the following clues: (1) The band is from a city outside of the United States (confirm the city explicitly), (2) The group originally had a different name but had to change it after discovering another group with the same name (the reason must be duplication/conflict, not a general rebrand), (3) The group credits another artist for giving or inspiring their final name (not a manager or label; a musician/artist is acceptable), (4) The group faced a documented tragedy (e.g., death of a member, severe accident, etc.) between Jan 1, 2020 and Dec 31, 2023, (5) Their debut EP was released between Jan 1, 2012 and Dec 31, 2018, and (6) They released something in 2019 (album, EP, single, or music video) that was named after something connected to their hometown (e.g., a local landmark, neighborhood, street, nickname, area code, or any clearly hometown-linked reference). Task: Build a comprehensive candidate list of any bands meeting most or all clues. For each candidate: provide (a) band name, (b) origin city and country, (c) details and sources proving the original name and the specific reason for the name change (duplicate), (d) evidence that another artist suggested or inspired their final name (with source), (e) details of the tragedy with exact date and source, (f) discography evidence for the debut EP and its release date (source), and (g) details of the 2019 release and how it connects to their hometown (source). Include direct links to sources (news articles, interviews, official statements, discographies). If no band satisfies all clues, include partial matches and explicitly list which clues are confirmed vs. uncertain for each. Consider English and non-English sources (UK, Europe, Asia, Latin America, etc.), and include at least 8–12 plausible candidates before narrowing. Avoid speculation; focus on documented evidence.
